> Thanks Kate — appreciate the quick review and the annotated MSA. Looping in Markus from Legal and Marissa (your AE) plus Naomi from CS for ramp details.

I reviewed Granite’s redlines. Summary of proposed internal positions (high level):
1) Section 7 (Data residency): we can accept a narrow carveout limited to customer-originated PII subject to GDPR/CCPA retention requests, but we cannot agree to a geographically-restricted hosting obligation that prevents failover in emergency scenarios. Proposed compromise language attached (MSA_counter_Sec7.txt).
2) Section 12 (Indemnity and Cap): we will propose that the overall liability cap remains at 12 months' fees (consistent with Redwood policy) but add a narrowly tailored carveout for third-party IP claims and for gross negligence/bad faith.

I have drafted redline suggestions and included rationale; please review and flag any business objections. If acceptable, I’ll send to Kate for a quick legal-to-legal sync.

Attachment: MSA_Granite_counter_Sec7-12.docx (proposed language and comment rationale)

- Markus
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference

Granite legal reviewed your counterlanguage and the team is comfortable with the compromise on Section 7 (narrow PII carveout + emergency failover language). On Section 12, they want to keep the cap numeric tie to 12 months' fees but asked for a defined process for escalation in the event of an IP claim; suggested: 30-day cure + meet-to-consider settlement before public filing.

Procurement confirms DocuSign is acceptable once legal language is finalized. Could you please: 1) incorporate the agreed language in a clean MSA v4 and 2) publish the final Order Form v3 clean version (no redlines) and send DocuSign package by next Wednesday 07/07?
